item.title: Temperature Dependence of Ductile Fracture in Structural Low-Carbon Steel

Abstract This study presents a temperature-dependent fracture model for predicting ductile crack initiation in low-carbon structural steel subjected to elevated temperatures. The continuum damage mechanics-based model is developed using data from twenty-five coupon tests on A572 Gr. 50 (345 MPa) steel on specimens with a wide range of stress triaxialities and Lode angle parameters over temperatures from 20°C to 700°C. Complementary finite element simulations replicate the stress–strain response up to fracture, while micromechanical void cell simulations provide insight into temperature-driven damage mechanisms. The experimental results show a systematic decrease in fracture strain with increasing temperature up to 600°C, attributed to diminished strain hardening leading to accelerated localization of plastic deformation at the microvoid scale. Void cell simulations corroborate these trends, demonstrating increased void growth rate and reduced localization strains at elevated temperatures. Based on these findings, the stress-weighted ductile fracture model (SWDFM) is extended to incorporate temperature dependence under varying stress triaxiality and Lode angle. The model is calibrated using the new experimental data, validated across multiple specimen geometries and stress states, and assessed for robustness through cross-validation. Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) enables the manufacturing of complex Ti6Al4V components, but the resulting mechanical and fatigue responses are condition-dependent. This critical narrative review examines how alloy grade and interstitial chemistry, powder history, processing, microstructure, residual stress, defect population, surface condition and post-processing affect quasi-static behaviour and low-, high- and very-high-cycle fatigue behaviour. Reported properties are compared with the associated material and test data, including surface condition, build orientation, stress ratio, loading mode, stress definition and run-out criterion. The review distinguishes finite-life fatigue strength from a demonstrated fatigue limit and separates stress-life data from strain-life and crack-growth parameters. The resulting condition-specific synthesis is intended to support engineering comparison and numerical modelling without treating LPBF Ti6Al4V as a single universal material dataset. item.title: Enhanced impact toughness through martensitic substructure refinement in a 30Cr2Ni3Mo2CoV secondary hardening steel via quenching–cryogenic–quenching–tempering treatment
item.description: 库内相似论文：A study on the plasticity and fracture of the AISI 4340 steel alloy under different loading conditions and considering heat-treatment effects（相似度 0.744） 温度效应与热软化: 可作为温度项形式、软化机制与绝热升温修正的建模参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对温度区间、加热方式、是否等温、绝热升温是否已修正 仅题名片段: Enhanced impact toughness through martensitic substructure … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 公开阅读反馈 直接有用: https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Substructure%E2%80%93enabled+dynamic+strain+aging+and+%CE%BA-carbide+nano-precipitation+in+a+high-SFE+F&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.matdes.2026.117446%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22strain_rate%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Classical theories predict that dynamic-strain-aging (DSA) should be strongly suppressed in high stacking-fault-energy (SFE) Fe–Mn–Al–C steels, because narrow, temperature-sensitive stacking-fault widths limit solute–dislocation interaction times. Contrary to these expectations, we demonstrate that a high-SFE lightweight steel exhibits pronounced DSA from 100-to-500 °C, a regime traditionally considered unlikely. Despite serrated-flow and negative strain-rate-sensitivity, the alloy retains remarkably stable ductility and work-hardening capability, revealing a fundamentally non-classical DSA response that is not governed by conventional stacking-fault-mediated solute–dislocation interactions. Electron-backscatter-diffraction shows rapid formation of a boundary-rich substructure consisting of dense low-angle-boundaries and refined subgrains that concentrate mobile dislocations at interfaces. This deformation-generated-network acts as a fast-diffusion scaffold that enables stress-assisted pipe and boundary diffusion of interstitial and substitutional solutes, activating a DSA mechanism independent of stacking-fault-mediated interactions. Transmission electron microscopy and selected-area diffraction reveal ordering-like nanoscale domains consistent with deformation-assisted short-range-ordering near 300 °C and a transition to κ-carbide(L′1 2 ) nanoprecipitation above 500 °C, indicating that deformation-induced solute redistribution associated with the DSA regime may facilitate subsequent κ-phase formation at higher temperatures. These findings uncover a previously unreported substructure-assisted DSA mechanism in high-SFE steels, explain the coexistence of strong DSA and sustained ductility, and establish a mechanistic link between warm-temperature DSA, dynamic ordering, and κ-carbide precipitation. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Strain+Localization%2C+Damage+Evolution%2C+and+Fracture+Mechanisms+in+Sheet-Metal+Bending%3A+A+R&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.3390%2Fmet16111234%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22ductile_fracture%22%2C+%22damage_evolution%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Sheet-metal bending produces pronounced through-thickness strain gradients and localized deformation. The resulting damage and fracture depend on microstructure, specimen geometry, loading path, and failure criterion. This review examines bending configurations, stress and strain distributions, neutral-layer evolution, bendability measures, and multiscale characterization methods, and compares damage behavior in steel, aluminum, copper, magnesium, and titanium alloys. It then considers damage initiation and crack propagation in relation to surface roughening and strain localization, slip and shear bands, second phases and interfacial damage, and twinning and tension–compression asymmetry. Most studies describe bending damage in different metals through related stages of heterogeneous microscale deformation, strain localization, damage initiation, and crack propagation. Microstructural heterogeneity and initial defects govern local deformation compatibility, while geometry and processing conditions affect strain gradients, constraint, and damage accumulation. Limit bend angle, minimum bend radius, and load-drop point are apparent measures determined jointly by the material, specimen, and process; none directly measures intrinsic fracture resistance. Bendability should therefore be evaluated using local strain fields, crack evidence, and microstructural evolution together. The review provides guidance for material selection, bending-test design, model calibration, and the definition of safe processing windows, while identifying in situ multiscale characterization, microstructure-informed damage modeling, AI-assisted damage prediction, and standardized bendability assessment as priorities for future research. This study establishes a high-accuracy machine learning framework for predicting flow stress in 2124 Al/10% SiCp composites during hot deformation. Eight advanced algorithms—including XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, and an Enhanced Ensemble model—were thoroughly optimized and evaluated using experimental data spanning 300–500 and strain rates of 0.001–1.0 . Physics-informed feature engineering, centered on the Zener–Hollomon parameter, significantly enhanced prediction accuracy. The XGBoost model achieved exceptional performance ( = 0.9985, MAPE = 3.26%), outperforming traditional regression by 75% and fuzzy logic by 46%. Interpretability analysis confirmed the dominance of thermally activated deformation mechanisms, validating the physical consistency of the models. The predicted flow stresses enabled the development of reliable processing maps, identifying optimal hot working conditions at 400–450 and 0.01–0.1 . This work demonstrates a robust, interpretable, and industrially applicable data-driven approach for optimizing the thermomechanical processing of metal matrix composites. To address the insufficient understanding of the surface plastic deformation mechanism of Ti-6Al-4V alloy during ultrasonic surface rolling processing (USRP), this study adopts an approach combining finite element (FE) simulation and molecular dynamics (MD) analysis. The effects of static load, ultrasonic vibration frequency, and ultrasonic amplitude on residual stress and surface plastic deformation are investigated, and the dislocation evolution and local deformation response under ultrasonic vibration are analyzed at the atomic scale. A three-dimensional explicit dynamic FE model based on the Johnson-Cook constitutive law is established to examine the variations of surface residual stress, equivalent plastic strain, and plastic displacement under different static loads, ultrasonic vibration frequencies, and ultrasonic amplitudes, and the validity of the FE model is verified against experimentally measured residual stress results. The results show that static load is the dominant factor governing the degree of macroscopic surface plastic deformation. Within the investigated static-load range of 100–400 N, the magnitude of the peak residual compressive stress increases overall from 685.11 MPa to 722.09 MPa, although the variation is not strictly monotonic, while the maximum PEEQ increases from 0.12481 to 0.38641 and the affected depths increase markedly. Increasing the ultrasonic amplitude further enhances near-surface plastic deformation, whereas the influence of ultrasonic vibration frequency on macroscopic plastic deformation is relatively limited within the 20–29 kHz range. On this basis, a simplified Ti-Al atomic model of the α phase of Ti-6Al-4V alloy is established to analyze the effect of ultrasonic vibration on atomic-scale plastic deformation behavior by comparing the dislocation evolution, loading force, and system potential energy under conditions with and without ultrasonic vibration. The MD results indicate that periodic excitation is accompanied by an increase in the number and total line length of detected dislocations, together with lower time-averaged indentation reaction forces and higher reported potential-energy values under the investigated simulation conditions. These observations suggest that periodic excitation modifies local defect evolution and indentation response within the simplified atomic model, providing complementary insights into atomic-scale plastic deformation. This study can provide a reference for process optimization and surface strengthening mechanism research of Ti-6Al-4V alloy during USRP. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Energy-saving+optimized+parameters+for+3D+selective+laser+melting+using+dimensionless+mode&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1108%2Frpj-01-2026-0038%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22lpbf_tc4%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Purpose This study aims to identify energy-efficient selective laser melting (SLM) parameters that achieve high relative density and mechanical performance while reducing trial-and-error experiments. Design/methodology/approach The proposed workflow integrates dimensionless process mapping, an analytical melt-pool geometry model, specific energy consumption (SEC, Es) evaluation, and an artificial neural network (ANN) surrogate map. For Ti6Al4V, the selected parameter set was further evaluated by increasing hatch spacing based on powder-entrainment and melt-pool-width considerations, followed by density and tensile tests. The same SEC-guided screening strategy was also applied to an IN718 dataset to check cross-material applicability. Findings For Ti6Al4V at 80 µm hatch spacing, the optimized condition achieved 99.98% relative density, 1201 MPa tensile strength and 8.2% elongation. The experimentally assessed 120 µm energy-efficient hatch-spacing extension reduced model-estimated SEC by 36.2% while maintaining 99.95% relative density. Tensile strength increased to 1299 MPa, whereas elongation decreased to 6.22%, indicating a strength–ductility tradeoff. Originality/value This work proposes a physics-informed and data-assisted optimization workflow linking dimensionless modeling, melt-pool geometry screening, SEC-based energy evaluation, ANN surrogate mapping and experimental testing. Unlike approaches that apply dimensionless analysis or machine learning separately, the proposed method selects low-Es parameter sets within a physically constrained process window and assesses their density and tensile performance. Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables the fabrication of metallic components with complex geometries and high performance. However, achieving coordinated control of formability including defect suppression and cracking resistance together with mechanical properties such as strength, ductility, and fatigue life remains a critical challenge for LPBF alloys. Although artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely adopted for process optimization, defect prediction, and performance evaluation, conventional AI models often lack physical metallurgical interpretability, leading to limited generalization and unreliable extrapolation beyond training domains. This review focuses on the role of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) in addressing the formability–performance trade-off in LPBF alloys. We first introduce four knowledge domains that establish physical interpretability in metallic materials: physical metallurgy principles, cross-scale numerical information, microstructure image analysis, and causal physical mechanisms. Subsequently, we systematically examine XAI applications across representative LPBF alloy systems. In performance-oriented alloys such as steels and titanium alloys, XAI facilitates mechanism–aware control of non-equilibrium phase transformations, microstructural anisotropy, and defect-sensitive fatigue behavior. In formability-oriented alloys including aluminum alloys and nickel-based superalloys, XAI supports cracking susceptibility prediction, process–window identification, and printable alloy design. Despite these advances, most current studies remain task-specific and single-objective, with limited integration of formability and performance optimization. To overcome this limitation, we propose a unified multi-objective optimization framework incorporating physically constrained modeling, standardized multimodal databases, and causal reasoning. This review provides guidance for the intelligent, reliable, and collaborative design of LPBF alloys with both high formability and excellent mechanical performance. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Microstructure-controlled+nanoscale+deformation+and+scratch-induced+damage+evolution+in+a+&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.jmrt.2026.10.262%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22ductile_fracture%22%2C+%22damage_evolution%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Understanding the relationship among microstructure, deformation, and damage evolution is essential for evaluating the scratch response of high-entropy alloys (HEAs). In this study, a TiVAlNbHfCr HEA fabricated by spark plasma sintering (SPS) was investigated to elucidate the influence of microstructure on nanoscale deformation and scratch-induced damage. CALPHAD (Thermo-Calc, TCHEA2) calculations predicted BCC_2 and HCP_A3 as equilibrium phases, with an Al 3 Zr 4 -labelled (Zr 4 Al 3 -type) intermetallic at lower temperature, whereas XRD of the SPS-consolidated alloy indicated a BCC matrix with NbAl 3 and Ti 3 Al-type secondary phases; the calculation is therefore used as a qualitative guide to phase stability rather than as a prediction of the as-sintered constitution. Nanoindentation yielded a hardness (H_IT) of 7.49 ± 0.82 GPa and an indentation modulus (E_IT) of 155.10 ± 10.99 GPa, while the (H/E) and (Hˆ3/Eˆ2) ratios indicated high elastic strain tolerance and resistance to plastic deformation. Scratch testing identified distinct elastic, plastic, and failure regimes, demonstrating that microstructural heterogeneity influences strain localization, pile-up formation, and crack initiation. A physics-guided analysis was subsequently used to relate the experimentally measured mechanical and scratch-response parameters to the observed deformation and damage behavior. The analysis does not yield wear rates, wear life, or service-life predictions. Bootstrap resampling of the 16 nanoindentation measurements was used to quantify sampling uncertainty in the indentation-derived parameters. Bootstrap resampling was used to quantify variability and uncertainty in the derived relationships. Overall, the combined experimental, CALPHAD-guided, and physics-informed analysis provides a mechanistic framework for interpreting microstructure-dependent nanoscale deformation and scratch-induced damage in TiVAlNbHfCr HEA. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Relationship+between+characteristics+of+local+deformed+state+and+damage+parameters+of+stru&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.17073%2F0368-0797-2026-5-526-534%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22plasticity_hardening%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Tensile tests were performed on the samples with stress concentrators made of structural steels of 20 and 45 grades, with an analysis of the local deformed state using the digital image correlation method and damage assessment by optical microscopy. Strain dependences were plotted for the areas of the plastic deformation zone S Y , the values of the principal strain ε 1 , and the damage parameter S * , defined as the relative area of microcracks in the image. The authors analyzed the stage-wise fracture of the studied specimens and proposed a metho­dology for calculating the total damage S tot in the plastic zone, based on the experimentally established relationship between damage and value of the principal strain. It was established that under loading, microcrack initiation in steel 45 occurs at an earlier fracture stage compared to steel 20. At the same time, at the final loading stage, the growth rate of the total microcrack area S tot in steel 20 specimen is higher than in steel 45 sample, which is reflected in the exponent of the strain dependence of S tot , which is almost twice as high as the corresponding parameter for steel 45 ( m = 5.5 and 2.97, respectively). The observed differences in damage kinetics are associated with the strain-hardening coefficient and structure of the studied steels. The approach applied in this study can be used for structural integrity diagnostics, as it allows evaluating of material damage over a larger surface area of the structural element compared to optical microscopy, which has limitations on the size of the investigation area and imposes high requirements on quality of the studied surface preparation. Phase-field damage modelling (PFDM) has emerged as an effective framework for simulating a material degradation and failure processes due to its ability to predict the evolution of damage. In this study, a 2D axisymmetric PFDM formulation is verified in PAK-DAM FEM software through comparison with 3D solid model for benchmark example from the literature. After that, 2D axisymmetric FE model is used for a comparison with experimental tensile tests of high-strength S1100QL steel. The finite element model is developed using 2D axisymmetric elements, incorporating large-strain von Mises plasticity with a logarithmic strain constitutive model. The FE mesh consists of 970 elements and 1078 nodes, with boundary and loading conditions defined to replicate the experimental setup. A comparison of stress-strain response obtained from numerical simulations and experimental measurements shows good agreement, confirming the capability of the proposed PFDM approach to accurately reproduce the tensile behaviour of metallic materials such as S1100QL steel. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Rapid+Evaluation+of+Chaboche%E2%80%93Voce+Material+Model+Parameters+Through+a+Fully+Reversed+Strai&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.3390%2Fma19214735%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22plasticity_hardening%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Modeling cyclic plasticity remains challenging due to the high computational cost of nonlinear constitutive models and the large number of parameters requiring evaluation, which are often temperature-dependent. This work presents a systematic procedure for identifying the parameters of the Chaboche–Voce model, one of the most widely adopted constitutive models for cyclic plasticity and commonly implemented in finite element software. Due to its nonlinear formulation, however, parameter evaluation is not straightforward. The parameters governing the kinematic hardening response are determined through a simple least-squares fit, yielding an analytical expression for a branch of the mid-life stabilized cycle. The Voce parameters are subsequently obtained by solving an analytical equation followed by a further least-squares fit. The resulting methodology provides a systematic approach for characterizing materials exhibiting both cyclic hardening and softening. The procedure was applied to two materials: 42CrMo4+QT tested at room temperature at different strain ranges for two different values of mean strain and 1Cr-1Mo-0.25V steel tested at different temperatures and strain ranges. The proposed approach provides satisfactory constitutive parameters while requiring virtually negligible computational cost, making it suitable for efficient material characterization and subsequent finite element implementation. Ballistic impact is a terminal ballistic phenomenon wherein a high-velocity projectile interacts with armour or protective systems, leading to material deformation, disintegration and perforation. This study investigates the ballistic impact response of KFRP and epoxy layered targets subjected to rigid and deformable projectile cores extracted from 7N31 armour-piercing (AP) ammunition. Four target–projectile configurations are considered, comprising KFRP with epoxy and epoxy with KFRP target arrangements impacted by arne steel and copper-plated steel (Cu–Steel) projectiles. The simulations are performed using the finite element method (FEM) in ANSYS/Autodyn. In this ballistic impact analysis, the ammunition core is modelled as a projectile impacting the target at a velocity of 600 m/s. Composite targets comprising 3, 5, and 7 layers are considered, with epoxy volume fractions of 10%, 20%, and 30% in KFRP with epoxy targets, as well as KFRP volume fractions of 10%, 20%, and 30% in epoxy with KFRP targets. For all simulation cases, the target plates are clamped (fixed) along their edges. The study shows that velocity attenuation is greater in high-KFRP targets as the number of layers increases at constant volume, compared with high-epoxy configurations. Thus the lowest residual velocities were 491.921 m/s for the Arne projectile and 285.649 m/s for the Cu–Steel projectile, both occurring in the high-KFRP configuration. Furthermore, the higher deformability of the projectile results in a larger back-face perforation diameter across all target configurations compared with the more rigid projectile. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+New+microstructural+insights+on+the+mechanisms+underlying+crack+initiation+and+growth+in+h&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.addma.2026.105432%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22impact_validation%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 High-density (>99.9% bulk density) additively manufactured (AM) alloys persistently suffer from premature failure under mechanical loading, severely restricting their deployment in safety-critical applications. While this deficit is historically attributed largely to processing defects such as porosity or residual stresses, this study uncovers the fundamental role of as-built microstructure on damage tolerance in wrought and laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) austenitic stainless steel as a model material. Using a state-of-the-art in situ multimodal 3D synchrotron X-ray approach, we directly resolve the spatial evolution of dislocation densities and internal stress fields inside bulk samples during crack initiation, something veiled to conventional characterization methods. These data reveal that while the wrought material dynamically generates dislocations to form a stress-shielding process zone that blunts cracks, the AM microstructure rapidly exhausts the capacity for dislocation generation. This stagnation of local dislocation density forces abnormally high stresses to persist, driving premature crack initiation even without significant porosity. These findings demonstrate that the evolution of local plasticity plays a fundamental role in damage tolerance of high-density PBF-LB alloys, providing new 3D microstructural insights on improving reliability of AM structural alloys. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Phase-field+analysis+on+the+interfacial+damage+behavior+of+high-speed+bearings+under+impac&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.26599%2Ffrict.2026.9441331%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22damage_evolution%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Abstract Transient impact-sliding contacts between the cage and the guiding ring under starved lubrication severely threaten the structural reliability of high-speed aero-engine main bearings. Traditional analytical and implicit finite element methods struggle to capture the highly nonlinear competitive failure mechanisms at this dual-body interface due to severe convergence bottlenecks and non-realistic single-body simplifications. In this study, a novel, fully coupled thermo-elasto-plastic phase-field fracture framework is proposed to systematically investigate the asymmetric damage evolution between an M50 steel ring and an AISI 4340 steel cage. The simulation results reveal a profound synergistic coupling effect between the normal impact and tangential sliding velocities. Furthermore, a fundamental disparity in spatial damage morphology is observed: the high-hardness M50 ring exhibits surface-initiated, elastic-dominated incipient micro-damage localization, whereas the tougher 4340 cage accommodates kinetic energy through subsurface-initiated, volumetric, thermo-elasto-plastic flow. Crucially, an asymmetric competitive degradation mechanism governed by an interfacial thermal partition coefficient is uncovered. By purposefully channeling a substantial fraction of the frictional heat into the 4340 cage, the cage undergoes catastrophic thermal softening and massive yielding, autonomously acting as a thermodynamic sacrificial buffer. This mechanism dynamically absorbs the destructive impact energy, physically shielding the core M50 ring from severe fatigue fracture. The extracted damage transition phase diagram provides a robust, physics-based criterion for the advanced surface engineering and thermal management of aerospace bearings. ductile fracture [https://doi.org/10.1007/s10704-009-9422-8] 引用重点论文：A new model of metal plasticity and fracture with pressure and Lode dependence [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijplas.2007.09.004] https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+New+Model+for+Ductile+Fracture+of+Metal+Alloys.+I%3A+Monotonic+Loading&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1061%2F%28asce%29em.1943-7889.0001009%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22ductile_fracture%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 In the absence of geometrical constraints, ductile fracture has been identified as the predominant mode of failure for structural elements under extreme loads, the prediction of which still represents considerable challenges. Ductile fracture of metals has only recently been recognized to be dependent on both stress triaxiality and Lode angle parameter. In this study, a new fracture model that is dependent on both stress triaxiality and Lode parameter is proposed. The developed model is proposed for the case of monotonic loading and is applicable to a wide range of stress states. The extension of the model to reverse loading, with complex loading history, is addressed in a parallel paper. The developed criterion is evaluated against data extracted from a series of multistress states monotonic experimental results for various metals, and a strong correlation is evident between the proposed model and experimental results in the entire range of the tested stress states. A detailed parametric study is conducted in order to show the effect of the model’s parameters on the fracture map. Comparative study among popular ductile fracture criteria and the proposed model in their prevailing ranges is also performed. The results show that the newly developed criterion, featuring only three parameters, does not lag behind its counterparts in any stress triaxiality ranges. Published: 2015-09-23T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Journal of Engineering Mechanics 研究类型: 跨金属方法参考

This paper describes the development of a high-speed torsional testing machine and results obtained on the strain-rate dependent strength of copper at large shear strains. Test techniques and data obtained are intended to be useful in applications such as ballistics and machining. For copper, the results indicate positive strain hardening behavior to very large strains under low rate, isothermal conditions and the transition to adiabatic thermal softening, shear instability and localization (shear banding) at high rates.
